display_name: Shafer Vineyards One Point Five, Napa Valley

verified_facts.naming_origin: Named for the 'generation and a half' partnership between founder John Shafer and his son Doug, who worked together so long they said theirs wasn't a second-generation story but a generation and a half.
verified_facts.blend_2022: 92% Cabernet Sauvignon, 3% Petite Verdot, 3% Merlot, 2% Malbec
verified_facts.cooperage: 18 months in 100% new French oak barrels (Allier & Tronçais)
verified_facts.vineyard_sources: Multi-site: Shafer's hillside estate vineyards, 'Borderline' vineyard in Stags Leap District, and selected Napa Valley sites. NOT single-vineyard.
not_true: NOT a Bay Area joke about drive time

source: Official Shafer 2022 tech sheet PDF (shafervineyards.com)

display_name: Oyster Bay Chardonnay, Marlborough

verified_facts.winemaking: Fermented 50/50 in stainless steel and French barriques, 9 months on lees with bâtonnage, partial malolactic fermentation
verified_facts.vineyard_sources: Wairau, Renwick, and Brancott — shallow, sandy loams over gravels
verified_facts.naming_origin: Named after Oyster Bay on the tip of New Zealand's South Island in Marlborough. Reflects the maritime influence on the wines. Producer is Delegat family.

source: Official Oyster Bay website (oysterbaywines.com)

display_name: Penfolds Bin 2 Mataro, South Eastern Australia

verified_facts.cooperage: 9 months in French and American oak (new and seasoned hogsheads)
verified_facts.naming_origin: Bin 2 first released in 1960. Discontinued in Australia in 1970s during white wine boom, then revived. 'Bin' numbering system from Penfolds' barrel storage.
not_true: NOT 100% Mataro — it is primarily Shiraz with Mataro as secondary

source: Penfolds official tasting note PDF, wine-searcher, WineStatistics

display_name: Catena Zapata High Mountain Vines Malbec, Mendoza

verified_facts.cooperage: 11-13 months in French oak barrels (mix of first, second, and third-use)
verified_facts.vineyard_sources: Blended from high-altitude vineyards in Maipu, Lujan de Cuyo, Tupungato and San Carlos
verified_facts.winemaking: 5-day cold maceration at 48°F, fermentation 10-16 days, total maceration 19-22 days
verified_facts.naming_origin: Named for the family's pioneering work with high-altitude Malbec vineyards in Mendoza

source: Catena Zapata official website (catenazapata.com), CellarTracker

display_name: Cakebread Cellars Cuttings Wharf Chardonnay, Los Carneros

verified_facts.vineyard_sources: Single-vineyard: Cuttings Wharf Road Vineyard in Carneros, on a low ridge with shallow loamy soils
verified_facts.naming_origin: Named after the vineyard site on Cuttings Wharf Road in the Carneros district of Napa Valley
verified_facts.climate: Cool Pacific fog regularly blankets the vines at the southern end of Napa Valley
verified_facts.producer_notes: Cakebread purchased the Cuttings Wharf Road Vineyard in 2004. 56 acres on a low ridge in eastern Carneros. Planted to six different French Chardonnay clones. Haire loam soils.

source: Cakebread Cellars official website (cakebread.com)

display_name: Tyrrell's Vat 1 Semillon, New South Wales

verified_facts.cooperage: NO OAK — fermented in stainless steel, no oak fermentation or maturation
verified_facts.vineyard_sources: Short Flat vineyard, oldest block planted 1923. Dry-grown old vines.
verified_facts.naming_origin: Vat 1 was created in 1963 as a single-vineyard wine from Short Flat. The 'Vat' numbering refers to the original storage vessels.
verified_facts.release_policy: Not released until 5 years of age
verified_facts.awards: Australia's most awarded white wine — almost 5,500 medals and 330+ trophies
not_true: NOT oak-aged — any claim of oak is fabrication

source: Tyrrell's official website, auswinesonline, The Wine Independent

display_name: Paul Hobbs Richard Dinner Cuvée Agustina Chardonnay, Sonoma Mountain

verified_facts.cooperage: 90% new French oak
verified_facts.vineyard_sources: Single-vineyard: Richard Dinner Vineyard on Sonoma Mountain
verified_facts.naming_origin: Cuvée Agustina is named after Paul Hobbs' daughter, Agustina Hobbs. Richard Dinner Vineyard is the vineyard site name on Sonoma Mountain.

source: K&L Wines, Wine Spectator, Paul Hobbs Winery

display_name: d'Arenberg The High Trellis Cabernet Sauvignon, McLaren Vale

verified_facts.blend: Primarily Cabernet Sauvignon (exact blend varies by vintage)
verified_facts.cooperage: Av. 12 months in new and old French and American oak barriques and large casks. Basket pressed, barrel fermented on lees.
verified_facts.winemaker: Chester d'Arenberg Osborn (4th generation winemaker). Senior Winemaker: Jack Walton.
verified_facts.vineyard_sources: Old vines, some dating to 1912
verified_facts.naming_origin: The High Trellis vineyard was nicknamed because its vines were the first at d'Arenberg to be trained above knee-height in the 1890s
verified_facts.winemaking: Foot treading two-thirds through fermentation. No fining or filtration.
verified_facts.awards: Won Jimmy Watson trophy at 1969 Melbourne Wine Show (first vintage exhibited)

source: d'Arenberg official info, Langton's, Jancis Robinson

display_name: Vasse Felix Filius Cabernet, Margaret River

verified_facts.cooperage: 11 months in French oak
verified_facts.naming_origin: 'Filius' means 'son of' in Latin — it is the 'son of' the Vasse Felix flagship Cabernet, made from younger vines (average 20 years) in a more forward, earlier-drinking style
verified_facts.producer_history: Vasse Felix was established in 1967 by Dr Tom Cullity as Margaret River's founding wine estate

source: Vasse Felix official info, wine-searcher, Wine.com

display_name: Fritz Haag Brauneberger Juffer Sonnenuhr Riesling Auslese, Mosel

verified_facts.vineyard_sources: Juffer-Sonnenuhr — the steepest, most south-facing center cut of the Brauneberg hillside. Grosse Lage (Grand Cru equivalent). Pure southern slate site.
verified_facts.estate_history: Earliest documentation dates to 1605. Estate located in central Mosel River Valley.
verified_facts.pradikat: Auslese — rich, concentrated style with interplay between fruity sweetness and vibrant acidity
verified_facts.naming_origin: 'Sonnenuhr' means 'sundial' — referring to the sundial on the vineyard hillside. 'Juffer' is the vineyard name. 'Brauneberger' refers to the village of Brauneberg.

source: K&L Wines, Loosen Bros USA, Vinous, vinello.eu

display_name: Terroir Al Limit Les Tosses, Catalunya

verified_facts.cooperage: Varies by vintage: older vintages in 1200L Stockinger fuder (18-24 months), recent vintages ferment and age in cement tanks (8 months)
verified_facts.winemaker: Dominik Huber (co-founded with Eben Sadie in 2001; Sadie left 2011). Tatjana Peceric also key.
verified_facts.vineyard_sources: Les Tosses: steep, 90-year-old head-pruned vineyard on llicorella (slate) soil at 600m elevation, highest vineyard in Torroja del Priorat
verified_facts.naming_origin: Dominik discovered the vineyard while riding his motorbike on dirt roads around Torroja
verified_facts.winemaking: Whole cluster native fermentation, two weeks on skins, no wood aging (completely dispensed with new oak). Biodynamic farming.
not_true: NOT a blend — single varietal Cariñena
verified_facts.appellation: Priorat DOCa (Spain's highest quality classification, shared only with Rioja)

source: European Cellars, Terroir Al Limit official website, Berry Bros & Rudd

display_name: Comando G El Reventon, Cebreros

verified_facts.cooperage: 16 months in French oak
verified_facts.winemaker: Daniel Landi and Fernando García (childhood friends, founded Comando G 2008)
verified_facts.vineyard_sources: El Reventón: 1-hectare parcel of ~70-year-old Garnacha at 900m elevation on slate soils
verified_facts.naming_origin: 'El Reventón' is the vineyard/parcel name. In Spanish, 'reventón' means 'burst' or 'blowout', colloquially also a steep slope. Comando G is named for Garnacha.
verified_facts.note: El Reventón vineyard was sold to Adrianna Catena; last Comando G vintage was 2022

source: European Cellars, Decanter, Les Caves de Pyrene

display_name: Terre del Barolo Arnaldo Rivera, Barolo

verified_facts.cooperage: 20 months in French wood (25% used tonneaux, 50% 25hL oak casks, 25% 50hL oak casks)
verified_facts.vineyard_sources: Multi-site blend from Serralunga d'Alba, Castiglione Falletto, Diano d'Alba, La Morra, and Verduno
verified_facts.naming_origin: Arnaldo Rivera (1919-1987) was a primary school teacher, mayor of Castiglione Falletto for almost 40 years, Italian partisan, and founder of Cantina Terre del Barolo cooperative on December 8, 1958 with 22 founding members.
verified_facts.winemaking: 13 days skin fermentation in stainless steel, spontaneous malolactic in wood

source: Terre del Barolo official catalog, Wikipedia, Monsieur Touton

display_name: Leo Hillinger, Burgenland

verified_facts.vineyard_sources: 90+ hectares across Jois, Oggau, and Rust in Burgenland
verified_facts.producer_notes: Converted to organic practices in 2010. One of largest high-quality producers in Austria.
verified_facts.naming_origin: Named after the winemaker/owner Leo Hillinger

source: KW Selection, Artisanal Cellars, Falstaff

display_name: des Bosquets, Gigondas Les Routes

verified_facts.blend: 100% Syrah (Serine clone — old clone/relative of Syrah). Small-berried vines from bud wood originally from Gerard Chave via Jacques Reynaud's Château de Fonsalette.
verified_facts.cooperage: 18 months in oak casks (predominantly destemmed)
verified_facts.vineyard_sources: Les Routes vineyard: Serine clone Syrah on clay with gravel and limestone colluviums near the Hautes Garrigues
verified_facts.naming_origin: Les Routes is the vineyard/lieu-dit name
not_true: NOT a Grenache-based blend despite being Gigondas — this is a rare 100% Syrah from the appellation

source: European Cellars, Vinous, Wine Enthusiast

display_name: Montes Alpha M, Valle de Colchagua

verified_facts.blend: 80% Cabernet Sauvignon, 10% Cabernet Franc, 5% Merlot, 5% Petit Verdot
verified_facts.cooperage: 18 months in French oak (70% new)
verified_facts.winemaker: Aurelio Montes (co-founder). Current team includes Laura Catena-era collaboration. Wine only released with founder approval.
verified_facts.vineyard_sources: Apalta single estate in Colchagua Valley
verified_facts.naming_origin: 'Alpha M' is Montes' flagship/icon wine. The 'M' likely stands for Montes but this is not explicitly confirmed in official sources. First released in 1996, it put Chile on the map for premium Bordeaux blends.

source: Montes official website, Kobrand, Artisan W&S

display_name: Howard Park Leston Cabernet Sauvignon, Western Australia

verified_facts.cooperage: 18 months in French oak (40% new)
verified_facts.vineyard_sources: Leston Vineyard, Wilyabrup, Margaret River — free-draining gravelly loam over clay
verified_facts.naming_origin: Named after the Leston Vineyard site in Wilyabrup
verified_facts.cellaring: Drink now or cellar up to 15 years

source: Burch Family Wines official site, Langton's

display_name: Atamisque Chardonnay, Mendoza

verified_facts.cooperage: 10 months in French oak barrels
verified_facts.vineyard_sources: Single vineyard in San José area, Tupungato District, Uco Valley — 1,300m elevation, clay and sand alluvial soils
verified_facts.naming_origin: 'Atamisque' is the name of a native tree (Atamisquea emarginata) that grows naturally in the winery's surroundings in Mendoza

source: Atamisque official info, Mitchell & Son, WB Imports

display_name: Wind Gap Woodruff Vineyard Pinot Noir, Santa Cruz Mountains

verified_facts.vineyard_sources: Woodruff Vineyard: 9 acres near Coralitos, planted 1978. Originally Matteson, then Ciardella, renamed Woodruff 1991.
verified_facts.naming_origin: 'Wind Gap' refers to geological breaks in coastal hills that funnel wind inland — the winery celebrates this force that shapes their wines. Woodruff is the vineyard owner's name.
verified_facts.winemaking: Low brix picking, natural yeast, some whole cluster, aged in neutral French oak/concrete/stainless

source: Prince of Pinot, Wind Gap official website

display_name: Black Box Deep & Dark Cabernet Sauvignon, California

verified_facts.producer_notes: Black Box launched 2003 by Constellation Brands. Acquired by E&J Gallo in 2021. Central Valley California production. 3-liter boxed wine format (equivalent to 4 bottles).
verified_facts.naming_origin: 'Deep and Dark' is a marketing descriptor for the wine style — rich, dark fruit flavors

source: Fine Wine & Good Spirits, Marketview Liquor, Tastings.com

display_name: Barefoot Buttery Chardonnay, California

verified_facts.winemaker: Jennifer Wall (Chief Winemaker since 1995, 'most awarded winemaker in the world')
verified_facts.producer_history: Founded 1965 by Davis Bynum. Sold to Bonnie Harvey and Michael Houlihan 1986 (renamed Barefoot Cellars). Acquired by E&J Gallo 2005.
verified_facts.vineyard_sources: California Central Valley grapes
verified_facts.naming_origin: 'Buttery' is a style descriptor — the wine is made to emphasize creamy, buttery mouthfeel (likely through malolactic fermentation and/or oak)

source: Barefoot official website (barefootwine.com), Vinovest

display_name: Tolosa 1772 Grenache, Edna Valley

verified_facts.blend: 100% Grenache (from two vineyard sections: Poletti and Salaal)
verified_facts.cooperage: 15 months in French oak puncheons
verified_facts.vineyard_sources: Poletti section (higher elevation, afternoon sun) and Salaal section (velvety tannin structure)
verified_facts.naming_origin: '1772' is the year Mission San Luis Obispo de Tolosa was founded. The mission friars planted the first vineyards in the area.
verified_facts.winemaking: Mix of warm and cool fermentations, large oak puncheons

source: Tolosa Winery official tech sheet PDF, Wine History Project

display_name: Plantagenet Omrah Pinot Noir, Great Southern

verified_facts.cooperage: 10 months in French oak barrels
verified_facts.producer_history: Plantagenet established 1968, first commercial winery in Great Southern region (1975). Family-owned, Mount Barker.
verified_facts.vineyard_sources: 156 acres including Wyjup Vineyard with 50+ year old vines. Gravelly loam soils.
verified_facts.naming_origin: 'Omrah' is Plantagenet's second-label range — made from younger vineyards or bought-in fruit, offering value pricing. The etymology of the word 'Omrah' itself is not publicly documented. 'Plantagenet' refers to the Plantagenet Shire in Western Australia.
verified_facts.naming_note: 'Plantagenet' refers to the Plantagenet Shire in Western Australia where the winery is located

source: Plantagenet Wines official website, The Wine Society, Palmer's Wine

display_name: Kir Yianni Ramnista, Naoussa

verified_facts.cooperage: 18 months in 225L and 500L French and American oak casks, plus 6 months bottle aging
verified_facts.winemaker: Stellios Boutaris (son of founder Yiannis Boutaris)
verified_facts.vineyard_sources: Ramnista blocks at Kir-Yianni Estate, southeast exposure, 280-330m altitude
verified_facts.naming_origin: 'Ramnista' means 'royal hill' in local idiom, referring to the rolling hills of the Kir-Yianni Estate vineyard
verified_facts.winemaking: Hand-picked, sorted, 6-day cold soak, one-third in open-top tanks with pigeage

source: Kir-Yianni official website (kiryianni.gr), Skurnik Wines

display_name: Lafage Tessellae Vieilles Vignes, Cotes Catalanes

verified_facts.vineyard_sources: Old-vine Carignan on schist soils
verified_facts.naming_origin: 'Tessellae' refers to tesserae — the small tiles in Roman mosaics. The Roussillon region has significant Roman heritage.

source: Hachette, wine-searcher, Vivino

display_name: Lafage Tessellae Old Vines, Cotes du Roussillon

verified_facts.naming_origin: Named after Jeff Burch's father — Leston is a family name
